#### What this PR does / why we need it:

With cadvisor v0.39.0, the OOM parser correctly returns the container information for kernels >= 5.0. This PR has two aspects.

This allows us to expose the underlying cgroup OOM to the associated Pod resource by emitting an event. In addition, we should log the cgroup OOM in the kubelet logs.
- Adds cgroup OOM log message to Kubelet
- Adds the cgroup OOM event messages to the associated Pod resource.

Thanks for the PR, I agree it would great to have events for cgroup OOMs.

I'm not a big fan of using the same approach of relying on scraping dmesg logs to get OOMs. As we've seen in the past, this can be fragile and the log format can change across kernel versions.

For system OOMs that's the only option as far as I'm aware, but for cgroup OOMs there's a much more robust option: the kernel can report back when a cgroup OOMs via eventfd. See section 10 here: https://www.kernel.org/doc/Documentation/cgroup-v1/memory.txt

I believe the container runtime is already using this capability, for example containerd CRI will set the status to `OOMKilled` in case of OOM kill, see [here](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/4f181312393502a07b298b73dcdd379832612ecd/pkg/cri/server/events.go#L334-L350). This is all detected via the existing eventfd mechanism described above, implemented [here](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/4f18131/pkg/oom/v1/v1.go#L92)

Dockershim is also doing this and setting container status reason to `OOMKilled`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/dockershim/docker_container.go#L415

So I think the more robust approach here is to rely on the runtime to detect OOM Kill as opposed to scraping the dmesg logs. When kubelet finds out a container status has been updated with `OOMKilled` reason from the CRI, report that as a k8s event.

issue_context.title: Log and expose cgroup OOM events to the associated Pod resource
issue_context.body:
#### What happened:

Previously the cadvisor library had a regex parsing error, which resulted in it falling back to returning
a string character of `/` when parsing system oom messages on kernels >= 5.0. This was fixed in google/cadvisor#2813

~Since cadvisor was bumped in #99875, system OOM event messages are no longer being emitted because of the following line, where its checking that the `event.VictimContainerName == "/"`.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/e557f61784a90adf8dfe4a0bca875043e895cc8b/pkg/kubelet/oom/oom_watcher_linux.go#L75~

Since cadvisor was bumped in #99875, we can now retrieve the OOM'd pod id, creating a log entry and emit an event for the associated resource

#### What you expected to happen:

System OOM messages events to be emitted to the Node resource.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

Running a 1.21.x cluster, create a pod that OOM's.

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: memory-demo-2
  namespace: default
spec:
  containers:
  - name: memory-demo-2-ctr
    image: polinux/stress
    resources:
      requests:
        memory: "50Mi"
      limits:
        memory: "100Mi"
    command: ["stress"]
    args: ["--vm", "1", "--vm-bytes", "250M", "--vm-hang", "1"]
```

Observe that there is no SystemOOM message for the events of the node where that pod is running.

#### Anything else we need to know?:

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.21.0-beta.1.382+1a983bb958ba66
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration:
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): `Linux ip-172-31-48-224 5.4.0-1038-aws #40-Ubuntu SMP Fri Feb 5 23:50:40 UTC 2021 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux`
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:
comments: /sig node
/assign

Isn't this working as expected? A "system OOM" is not a cgroup level OOM, but rather a machine level OOM (https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/v5.11/mm/oom_kill.c#L1117-L1118). The example provided where a pod goes over the memory limit triggers a cgroup level OOM (not a system OOM), and as such the system OOM event should not be sent. This is why there is the explicit `event.VictimContainerName == "/"` check.

As you mentioned previously we were sending System OOM events unfortunately, but that was due a bug in the parsing of OOM messages, fixed in https://github.com/google/cadvisor/issues/2813

Hi @bobbypage, yes you are correct in that these are cgroup level OOM's that the provided example creates. I was more referring to the SystemOOM event message type, emitted as a Kubernetes event. Sorry about the confusion.

Prior to the v0.39.0 upgrade, cadvisor would always return `event.VictimContainerName == "/"`, even for cgroups for kernels >= 5.0. This can be verified by running the same example pod in a cluster prior to the v0.39.0 library update of cadvisor and checking the events on the associated node.

With the fix in google/cadvisor#2813, `event.VictimContainerName` will no longer return `/` for kernels >= 5.0 as it correctly parses the OOM message now, breaking the existing functionality of cgroup OOM event messages being emitted. I believe this is a regression.

Hi @kgtw

My understanding here is that `SystemOOM` k8s events should only be sent if there is a System OOM (_not_ a cgroup OOM). 

As you mentioned unfortunately, prior to  https://github.com/google/cadvisor/issues/2813 there was a bug on > 5.0 kernels such that the OOM parsing would consider cgroup OOMs as system OOMs and thus the cgroup OOMs were reported as SystemOOMs events incorrectly.

I don't believe kubelet ever reported events for cgroup OOMs at all (e.g. see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/69676 as a long running feature request). 

I believe if you test on a < 5.0 kernel (e.g. 4.19 LTS which is not affected by   https://github.com/google/cadvisor/issues/2813) you should see expected behavior which is that SystemOOM event is only sent if there is a system OOM not a cgroup OOM.

Thanks for the clarification. In that case I think it will make sense to update this issue & associated pr to be a feature request instead of a bug, which would cover some of the criteria in #69676. Specifically logs in kubelet, and emitting the event to the pod resource.

/remove-kind bug
/kind feature

The issue around silent pod-process OOM kills is a mess and comes biting in the ass over and over again, where a crucial pod-process that is not PID 1 dies and services go offline perfectly silently.  This happens with Selenium, Spark Operator, any JFrog chart, Couchbase and so, just to name a few.

1. It is very hard to identify what is the problem and where.
2. K8S can not do recovery. Let's say a Pod goes OOM every 2 days this way, a Pod restart would keep the service up, but in this case, it is just malfunctioning until someone gets his/her hands dirty to figure out the root cause.

I no longer have capacity available to address the PR comments for this to be merged as it would involve a significant rework. 

For those that are wanting a quick solution to the immediate problem, you can use the [oomie](https://github.com/kgtw/oomie) service which was the original inspiration for opening this issue/pr.
